exposure: biodiversity indices (species richness, net relatedness index, land-use types, freshwater fish species, stagnant water areas)
cohort: 109,233 child-mother dyads from the Japan Medical Data Center database, enrolled between January 2005 and January 2017.
finding: Greater species and genetic diversity of freshwater fish along with stagnant water areas were associated with a 2-5% lower risk of childhood asthma.
